package_info.package_name: N/A (RepoJacking vulnerability affects any package using renamed GitHub usernames)
package_info.package_manager: Go, Swift, Packagist (and any manager using GitHub URLs as source)
package_info.package_versions: All versions using vulnerable repository URLs (over 10,000 identified)
package_info.why_malicious: The vulnerability allows attackers to hijack the namespace of popular repositories after a username rename, enabling them to serve malicious code to users who depend on the original repository URL. This can result in widespread supply chain attacks.

malicious_snippets.code_language: any (depends on original repository language, e.g., Go, PHP, Swift, JavaScript, etc.)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When users or package managers fetch or install from the hijacked repository URL, the attacker's code is executed or included in the build, leading to arbitrary code execution or supply chain compromise.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Hijacking a popular repository namespace to serve attacker-controlled code is a classic supply chain attack vector.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Users expect the repository URL to always point to the original, trusted code. Instead, it now points to untrusted, potentially malicious code.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate repository transfers or renames, but not with the intent to deceive or hijack traffic.
key_indicators: Repository at a previously retired namespace suddenly reappears with new owner
Codebase changes drastically after namespace is reclaimed
Repository transfer and username rename sequence

attack_chain.action: Attacker registers the old username after it becomes available due to a rename.
attack_chain.leads_to: Ability to create a repository with the same name as the original popular project.

attack_chain.action: Attacker creates a repository with the same name as the original under the reclaimed username.
attack_chain.leads_to: Repository URL now matches the original, breaking the redirect and routing all traffic to the attacker's repository.

attack_chain.action: Attacker uploads malicious code to the hijacked repository.
attack_chain.leads_to: Users and package managers fetching from the original URL now receive and execute attacker-controlled code.

behavioral_signatures: Repository at a previously retired namespace is recreated by a new owner
Sudden change in repository ownership and codebase at a popular namespace
Repository transfer followed by username rename and acceptance of transfer
file_indicators: Repository content at a namespace with a history of high clone/download counts
Drastic codebase changes in a short time window
network_indicators: Package manager requests to GitHub URLs that have recently changed ownership
CI/CD pipelines pulling from GitHub repositories with recent namespace changes
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for recreation of repositories at previously retired or popular namespaces, especially following a username rename. Alert on sudden changes in repository ownership or codebase for high-profile projects. Track package manager or CI/CD fetches from GitHub URLs that have recently changed ownership or content. Use tools to verify the integrity and provenance of dependencies, and prefer immutable references (commit hashes) over mutable URLs.
